The present patent provides a method for improving the construction process of a wide-base radial truck tire. This improvement is achieved through the design of the carcass ply, the tire belt drum, and the tire semi-finished components. As a result, the durability and operability of the tire are improved.

It significantly improves the consistency between the finished tire and the theoretical tire material distribution design, thereby reducing the tire development cycle and development costs.

The improvement is achieved through the optimized design of the carcass ply, the tire belt drum, and the tire’s semi-finished components. It addresses the issue of carcass deformation and offers theoretical direction as well as technical support for improving the performance of wide-angle radial tires.

The proposed design approach for the belt drum used in the tire-building machine allows effective control of belt cord elongation. It also removes the problem of uneven stress distribution among the belt cords, preventing abnormal movement of the shoulder rubber of wide-base tires toward the center of the crown during shaping. The patent describes a method for improving the construction process of wide-base radial truck tires by optimizing the design of the carcass ply, the tire belt drum, and the tire semi-finished components. By coordinating these key structural and process elements, the method enhances the precision and stability of tire building, ensuring that the finished tire better meets performance and manufacturing requirements.

A major advantage of the method is that it addresses the problem of carcass bending during the construction and shaping process. Carcass bending can negatively affect tire uniformity, structural stability, and overall performance. By improving the carcass ply design and providing a more suitable construction process, the method offers both theoretical guidance and practical technical support for improving the performance of wide-base radial truck tires.

The patent also introduces an improved belt drum design. This design effectively controls the elongation of the belt cords during tire building and shaping. As a result, it helps eliminate uneven force distribution among the belt cords, which is important for maintaining belt stability, improving tire uniformity, and ensuring reliable tire performance under heavy-duty operating conditions.

In addition, the process prevents abnormal flow of shoulder rubber toward the crown center during shaping. Such undesired rubber flow can lead to uneven material distribution, structural defects, and reduced durability. By controlling the movement of rubber materials during the shaping stage, the method improves tire durability and makes the manufacturing process easier and more stable to operate.

Furthermore, the semi-finished component design method improves the accuracy of material distribution within the tire structure. More accurate material placement reduces the need for repeated trial production and adjustment during tire development. This not only shortens the development cycle of wide-base radial truck tires but also lowers development and manufacturing costs.

Overall, the patent provides a comprehensive technical solution for improving the manufacturing quality, process stability, and performance of wide-base radial truck tires. Through optimized structural design and process control, it enhances tire durability, uniformity, and production efficiency while reducing development time and cost.
outputs.L4:
This patent relates to the manufacture and structural design of wide-base radial truck tires, particularly tires intended to replace dual-tire arrangements on heavy-duty vehicles. Wide-base radial truck tires present unique construction challenges because their large section width and heavy load-bearing requirements can cause deformation during assembly, uneven stress distribution, and reduced durability if the carcass, belt package, and rubber components are not accurately controlled.

The invention improves the design of the carcass ply, the tire belt drum, and related semi-finished tire components in order to enhance both manufacturing stability and finished tire performance. By optimizing the carcass ply structure and its placement during tire building, the invention reduces excessive bending of the carcass, especially in regions where deformation can occur during shaping and curing. This helps maintain the intended tire profile and improves the accuracy of the final tire geometry.

The patent also addresses the behavior of belt cords during manufacture. In wide-base tires, the belt package is especially important because it must provide strength, stability, and uniform load distribution across a broad tread surface. The proposed design helps control belt cord elongation and improves force uniformity, reducing variations that can otherwise lead to uneven wear, belt separation, or localized stress concentration. A more uniform belt structure contributes to improved durability and better running performance under heavy loads.

In addition, the invention prevents abnormal flow of shoulder rubber during tire forming and vulcanization. The shoulder region of a wide-base radial truck tire is particularly sensitive because it is subjected to high stress, heat buildup, and repeated flexing during use. Uncontrolled rubber flow in this area can cause irregular shapes, structural imbalance, or defects that negatively affect service life. By improving the configuration of semi-finished components and the supporting drum structure, the invention helps maintain proper material distribution in the shoulder area.

Overall, the patent provides a more reliable method and structure for producing wide-base radial truck tires. It improves tire durability, manufacturing operability, and design precision while reducing development time and production cost. The result is a tire that can be built more consistently, performs more reliably in demanding truck applications, and offers improved efficiency for tire manufacturers.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it has great importance. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean one particular book that the speaker and listener both know about.

This simple word gives clarity to communication. It points to a person, place, object, or idea that is already known or unique. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky. We say “the teacher” when we are referring to a specific teacher.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it plays an essential role in making sentences clear and meaningful. Without it, English would sound less natural and more confusing. This small word shows how even the simplest parts of language can have a big effect.

counterfactuals.prompt: Please generate an abstract-style description for a tire manufacturing patent that solves carcass bending and uneven belt cord force problems in wide-base radial truck tires.
counterfactuals.output:
A wide-base radial truck tire is disclosed that improves carcass durability and belt uniformity by suppressing carcass bending deformation and reducing uneven force distribution in belt cords. The tire includes a radial carcass extending between bead portions, a belt reinforcing layer disposed radially outside the carcass, and a tread portion having an enlarged width suitable for wide-base heavy-duty use. The carcass profile, belt arrangement, and shoulder-region reinforcement are configured so that, under inflation and load, excessive bending of the carcass in the region from the tread shoulder to the sidewall is restrained. The belt structure includes a plurality of belt plies having selected cord angles, widths, and edge positions to distribute tension more uniformly across the belt, particularly near belt edges where stress concentration commonly occurs.  

By optimizing the relationship between carcass curvature, maximum tire width position, belt edge location, and tread ground-contact width, deformation of the crown and shoulder portions is controlled during rolling. This reduces localized strain, suppresses separation at belt ends, and prevents irregular belt cord loading caused by the increased tread width of wide-base radial tires. As a result, the tire provides improved resistance to belt-edge separation, enhanced carcass fatigue life, stable ground-contact pressure distribution, and improved durability for heavy-duty truck and bus applications.

The patent’s technical effects can be summarized as improvements to the molding/curing process and final quality of wide-base radial tires, especially by controlling geometry, material flow, and reinforcement behavior during building and vulcanization.

1. **Belt drum design for wide-base tire forming**
   - The belt drum is configured to better support and shape the wide belt/tread package used in wide-base radial tires.
   - It improves the accuracy of belt positioning, tread centering, and crown profile formation.
   - This helps reduce deformation, wrinkles, belt edge misalignment, and uneven expansion during shaping.
   - The result is improved uniformity, better tire roundness, and more stable high-speed performance.

2. **Control of cord elongation**
   - The invention manages elongation of reinforcing cords, especially in belt or carcass layers, during tire building and curing.
   - By limiting excessive cord stretch, the tire maintains the intended cord angle, belt width, and reinforcement distribution.
   - This reduces changes in tire dimensions after vulcanization and helps prevent non-uniform stiffness.
   - The effect is improved dimensional accuracy, reduced radial force variation, and enhanced durability.

3. **Prevention of shoulder rubber flow**
   - Wide-base radial tires have large shoulder regions where rubber can flow undesirably during molding and curing.
   - The patent addresses this by controlling rubber placement, restricting flow paths, or using structural features that stabilize the shoulder area.
   - This prevents shoulder rubber from migrating into unwanted regions, thinning locally, or causing bulges and voids.
   - The result is improved shoulder shape, reduced defects, better tread edge durability, and more uniform ground contact pressure.

4. **Material distribution of semi-finished parts**
   - The patent improves how semi-finished components—such as tread rubber, sidewall rubber, belt layers, innerliner, cushion rubber, and shoulder inserts—are arranged before curing.
   - Proper distribution ensures that rubber volume is placed where it is needed before mold closing and expansion.
   - This reduces excessive local accumulation or shortage of material during vulcanization.
   - The technical effect is improved tire balance, reduced scrap rate, better mold filling, and improved consistency between finished tires.

Overall, the patent improves the manufacturing accuracy of wide-base radial tires by coordinating drum geometry, reinforcement elongation, shoulder flow control, and pre-cure material placement. These measures help produce tires with better uniformity, stable belt structure, fewer molding defects, improved durability, and more reliable performance under heavy-load conditions.

## Patent Overview: Enhanced Wide-Base Radial Truck Tire Architecture and Manufacturing System

### Title  
**Wide-Base Radial Truck Tire Having Improved Carcass Ply, Belt Drum Construction, and Semi-Finished Component Configuration for Enhanced Durability, Operability, and Development Efficiency**

### Technical Field  
The invention relates to pneumatic radial tires for heavy-duty vehicles, and more particularly to wide-base radial truck tires having improved carcass reinforcement, belt package formation, and semi-finished component design. The invention further relates to tire-building methods and tire-building drum configurations that improve dimensional accuracy, structural durability, manufacturing repeatability, and design-development efficiency.

---

## Background

Wide-base radial truck tires are commonly used to replace dual tire assemblies in commercial trucking applications. By reducing vehicle weight, improving fuel efficiency, and enabling more efficient load distribution, wide-base tires provide substantial operational advantages. However, because a single wide-base tire must carry loads previously distributed across two tires, such tires are exposed to high deflection, severe lateral loading, increased crown stress, and elevated shoulder fatigue.

Conventional wide-base radial truck tires may suffer from one or more of the following issues:

1. **Carcass ply deformation or instability** under high load and low inflation conditions.  
2. **Belt edge separation** caused by uneven strain distribution near the belt shoulders.  
3. **Non-uniform crown geometry** due to limitations in belt drum expansion and component placement.  
4. **Reduced tire durability** under long-haul, regional, and mixed-service operation.  
5. **Manufacturing variation** arising from inconsistent semi-finished component dimensions or placement.  
6. **Long development cycles** caused by repeated trial-and-error adjustment of tire components, tooling, and building specifications.

Accordingly, there is a need for a wide-base radial truck tire and associated manufacturing system that improves tire performance, durability, and operability while reducing the number of prototype iterations and shortening development time.

---

## Summary of the Invention

The disclosed invention provides a wide-base radial truck tire, a tire belt drum, and semi-finished tire component configuration designed to improve structural stability, fatigue resistance, uniformity, and manufacturing efficiency.

In one embodiment, the tire includes an optimized carcass ply structure extending between bead regions and passing through sidewall and crown portions. The carcass ply may include selected cord angles, ply turn-up geometry, bead reinforcement, ply edge positioning, or material properties selected to control deformation of the wide tire casing during loaded operation.

In another embodiment, a tire belt drum is configured to form a belt package for a wide-base radial truck tire with improved crown contour, belt placement accuracy, and belt edge control. The belt drum may include a modified axial width, expandable segments, controlled crown curvature, shoulder shaping portions, or reference features for aligning belt layers and cap or cushion components.

In another embodiment, semi-finished tire components, including carcass ply strips, belt layers, sidewall strips, innerliner, shoulder cushions, gum strips, chafer components, apexes, or tread base components, are designed with controlled dimensions and profiles that correspond to the final tire architecture. Such semi-finished components reduce adjustment during tire building and vulcanization, thereby shortening development cycles and improving production repeatability.

The combined carcass ply, belt drum, and semi-finished component design provides a wide-base radial truck tire exhibiting improved durability, reduced shoulder separation, enhanced casing stability, improved retreadability, better high-speed and high-load performance, and more consistent operability across commercial vehicle applications.

---

## Representative Inventive Concepts

### 1. Improved Carcass Ply Structure

The carcass ply may be designed to provide increased stability across the wide crown and sidewall region of the tire. In a wide-base radial truck tire, carcass deformation is more pronounced than in conventional narrower truck tires because the crown span is greater and the tire experiences increased bending and lateral displacement.

The improved carcass ply may include one or more of the following features:

- A radial or substantially radial cord arrangement optimized for high-load truck service.  
- Steel, aramid, hybrid, polyester, or other high-modulus reinforcing cords.  
- A controlled ply turn-up height relative to the bead apex and sidewall flex zone.  
- A carcass ply profile selected to reduce strain concentration at the bead and lower sidewall.  
- Local reinforcement in shoulder or sidewall transition regions.  
- Controlled ply path curvature during building and curing to reduce residual stress.  
- Edge placement configured to avoid overlap with high-strain belt-edge regions.  
- A ply width and ply centerline alignment matched to the belt package and tread footprint.

By improving the carcass ply structure, the tire can maintain a more stable footprint, reduce casing distortion, improve steering response, and resist fatigue under repeated loading.

---

### 2. Optimized Belt Package Formation Using Improved Belt Drum

The belt drum used to assemble the belt package may be specifically configured for wide-base radial truck tires. Conventional belt drums may not adequately control the shape and placement of wide belt layers, particularly near belt shoulders, where edge lifting, wrinkles, trapped air, and uneven cord tension can contribute to separation.

The improved belt drum may include:

- A drum width corresponding to a wide-base crown package.  
- Expandable drum segments providing uniform radial expansion.  
- A crown-forming surface having a predetermined curvature.  
- Shoulder support regions that control belt edge geometry.  
- Axial reference markings or mechanical alignment stops for precise belt placement.  
- Vacuum ports or holding features to stabilize belt layers during application.  
- Temperature-controlled or low-friction surfaces to improve component handling.  
- A segmented structure configured to avoid discontinuities in belt tension.  
- A profile corresponding to the desired cured crown geometry.

The belt drum may allow the belt package to be built closer to its final intended shape, reducing deformation during shaping and curing. This can improve belt cord alignment, reduce residual stress, and decrease the likelihood of belt-edge cracking or separation.

---

### 3. Semi-Finished Component Design

The invention also provides semi-finished components designed to cooperate with the carcass ply and belt drum geometry. Rather than using generic flat strips or components requiring significant adjustment during building, the semi-finished components may be pre-shaped, profiled, dimensionally controlled, or indexed to the tire architecture.

Semi-finished components may include:

- Carcass ply assemblies.  
- Belt plies.  
- Zero-degree or low-angle cap strips.  
- Shoulder cushion gum.  
- Innerliner sheets.  
- Sidewall strips.  
- Bead apexes.  
- Chafers.  
- Tread base and tread cap assemblies.  
- Edge strips or belt-end gum strips.  
- Mini-sidewall or wing components.

The components may include one or more of:

- Tapered cross-sectional profiles.  
- Variable gauge thickness.  
- Predefined splice angles.  
- Markings, grooves, or indexing features.  
- Edge treatments to reduce stress concentration.  
- Widths matched to belt drum datum locations.  
- Rubber compounds selected for heat resistance, adhesion, fatigue resistance, or low hysteresis.  
- Reinforcement orientation controlled for each tire size.

By designing the semi-finished components in conjunction with the carcass and drum architecture, the development process becomes more predictable. Component dimensions can be standardized across tire sizes or scaled using defined design rules, reducing prototype iterations.

---

## Performance Advantages

### Improved Durability  
The disclosed tire architecture distributes stress more evenly through the carcass, belt package, shoulder region, and bead area. This may reduce:

- Belt edge separation.  
- Shoulder cracking.  
- Carcass fatigue.  
- Bead area damage.  
- Irregular wear.  
- Heat buildup under high load.  
- Casing distortion.

### Enhanced Operability  
The wide-base radial truck tire may provide improved real-world performance, including:

- Better footprint stability.  
- Improved lateral stability.  
- Reduced rolling resistance.  
- Improved high-speed endurance.  
- Enhanced load-carrying capability.  
- Better resistance to curb impact and sidewall flex damage.  
- Improved retreadability due to casing integrity.

### Improved Manufacturing Repeatability  
The combined system of controlled carcass ply design, belt drum geometry, and semi-finished component specification reduces build variability. Potential benefits include:

- More accurate belt placement.  
- Reduced component wrinkling.  
- Reduced trapped air.  
- Improved splice consistency.  
- Better green tire uniformity.  
- Reduced cured tire non-uniformity.  
- Improved yield and lower scrap.

### Reduced Development Cycles  
Because the tire components and tooling are designed as a coordinated system, development can proceed using predefined scaling and correlation rules. This may reduce:

- Number of prototype builds.  
- Trial-and-error tooling modifications.  
- Tire-building process adjustments.  
- Curing-related shape corrections.  
- Laboratory and road-test iteration cycles.  
- Time required to introduce new wide-base tire sizes.

---

## Example Embodiment

In one exemplary embodiment, a wide-base radial truck tire includes a carcass ply extending from a first bead portion to a second bead portion and having steel radial cords arranged substantially perpendicular to the circumferential direction. The ply is turned up around each bead core and terminates at a height selected to avoid peak flex regions of the sidewall.

A belt package is disposed radially outward of the carcass ply and includes multiple belt layers having alternating cord angles. A belt-end cushion component is positioned adjacent to one or more belt edges to reduce interlaminar shear stress. A zero-degree cap or spiral-wound reinforcement may be applied over at least part of the belt package to improve high-speed stability and crown growth resistance.

The belt package is assembled on a belt drum having a crown-forming outer surface with a controlled axial curvature. The drum includes shoulder support portions that maintain belt edges in a desired radial and axial position during building. Alignment datums on the drum correspond to edges or centerlines of semi-finished belt components.

Semi-finished components used to build the tire include belt layers cut to predetermined widths, cushion strips having tapered profiles, and sidewall or tread components having gauges selected to produce a cured tire contour with reduced residual stress. The coordinated component and drum design enables the green tire to approximate the final cured configuration, reducing distortion during shaping and vulcanization.

---

## Possible Claim Themes

### Independent Tire Claim  
A wide-base radial truck tire comprising:

- A pair of bead portions;  
- A carcass ply extending between the bead portions;  
- A belt package disposed radially outward of the carcass ply;  
- A tread disposed radially outward of the belt package; and  
- At least one semi-finished component having a predetermined profile or placement coordinated with a belt drum contour;

wherein the carcass ply, belt package, and semi-finished component configuration reduce strain concentration in at least one of a shoulder region, belt-edge region, or bead region during loaded operation.

### Independent Belt Drum Claim  
A belt drum for forming a belt package of a wide-base radial truck tire, comprising:

- A radially expandable drum body;  
- A crown-forming outer surface having a predetermined axial curvature;  
- Shoulder support regions configured to support belt edges; and  
- Alignment features corresponding to semi-finished belt component placement;

wherein the belt drum forms the belt package in a geometry approximating a cured crown profile of the wide-base radial truck tire.

### Independent Method Claim  
A method of manufacturing a wide-base radial truck tire, comprising:

1. Providing a carcass ply having a predetermined width, cord orientation, and turn-up configuration;  
2. Forming a belt package on a belt drum having a crown contour and shoulder support regions;  
3. Applying semi-finished components having predetermined profiles corresponding to the carcass and belt package geometry;  
4. Assembling a green tire; and  
5. Vulcanizing the green tire;

wherein the coordinated carcass ply, belt drum, and semi-finished component design improves tire uniformity and reduces development iterations.

### Development-Cycle Reduction Claim Theme  
A tire design and manufacturing system in which semi-finished component dimensions are derived from a predefined relationship among tire section width, belt width, carcass ply path, and belt drum contour, thereby reducing prototype testing cycles required to produce a wide-base radial truck tire meeting durability and operability targets.

---

## Industrial Applicability

The invention is applicable to commercial vehicle tires, including long-haul, regional-haul, mixed-service, refuse, bus, trailer, and heavy-duty truck applications. The disclosed tire structure and manufacturing method are particularly useful for wide-base radial truck tires intended to replace dual tire assemblies while maintaining durability, casing integrity, retreadability, and stable road performance.

---

## Conclusion

The disclosed technology provides an integrated approach to wide-base radial truck tire design and production. By improving the carcass ply architecture, forming the belt package on a specially configured belt drum, and using dimensionally coordinated semi-finished components, the invention enhances tire durability, operational stability, manufacturing consistency, and development efficiency. The result is a wide-base radial truck tire capable of carrying heavy commercial loads with improved resistance to fatigue, separation, irregular wear, and production variability while reducing the time and cost required to bring new tire designs to market.
